query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Earlier studies of other self-lubricating material systems reported low coefficients of friction at 704 °C and favorable friction and wear behavior over broad temperature ranges. However, these results do not resolve the limited understanding of wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys, and effectiveness must be maintained as operating temperature, load, and environment vary. Formulate one hypothesis that identifies a single intervention without presupposing its class, explains its mechanism, predicts friction and wear relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, defines its temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, relates it to prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small volume fraction of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) into a CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy will enable adaptive, in-situ formation of a lubricious BN/B2O3-rich tribofilm that maintains a lower coefficient of friction and wear rate than the unmodified alloy across room temperature to 800 °C in air under moderate loads.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy, solution-annealed, fine-grained (~10–50 µm), polished to Ra ≤ 0.1 µm, no solid-lubricant phases present.
generation.intervention: Uniformly disperse 3–7 vol% hexagonal boron nitride platelets (0.5–5 µm lateral size, aspect ratio ≥5) within the CoCrFeNi matrix via powder metallurgy (mechanical alloying of elemental powders with h-BN followed by spark plasma sintering) to form a dense self-lubricating metal–ceramic composite.
generation.conditions: Dry to moderately humid air (relative humidity 10–60%), counterface alumina or Si3N4, normal load 5–20 N (Hertzian contact up to ~0.8–1.2 GPa depending on geometry), sliding speed 0.05–0.2 m/s, total sliding distance ≥1000 m, temperature swept isothermally at 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous or near-continuous tribofilm on the wear track comprised of smearing and reorientation of h-BN lamellae intermixed with its oxidation product B2O3 and native Co/Cr/Ni oxides, forming a layered, low-shear composite film.
generation.mechanism: At room temperature, h-BN’s lamellar structure shears easily, reducing interfacial shear strength and limiting adhesive transfer. As temperature increases, partial oxidation of BN yields a viscous B2O3 glass that wets asperities, fills valleys, and provides a low-shear, glassy lubricious layer. The film self-replenishes from near-surface BN particles, while the ceramic phase raises hardness locally and decreases plowing and third-body abrasion. Together, lamellar shear and viscous flow of B2O3 lower friction and stabilize wear across the full temperature range.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the starting CoCrFeNi alloy, the BN-dispersed composite will exhibit a lower and more stable coefficient of friction across 25–800 °C, with a reduction on the order of 30–50% averaged over the range, and a specific wear rate reduction of roughly 2–5×. The improvement persists as temperature increases, with no temperature in the tested range showing higher friction or wear than the baseline under the stated loads and environment.
generation.baseline: Unmodified CoCrFeNi tested under the same counterface, load, speed, atmosphere, and temperatures typically shows moderate-to-high friction with temperature-dependent variability and increasing wear as temperature rises due to oxide-scale evolution and adhesive/abrasive mechanisms.
generation.boundary: Effectiveness is expected in oxidizing air from 25 to 800 °C at moderate loads (≤20 N) and speeds (≤0.2 m/s). Performance may degrade under: very high humidity with liquid water present (hydrolysis and leaching of B2O3), extremely high contact pressures causing BN crushing or delamination (>~1.5 GPa Hertzian), highly reducing or chlorine-containing atmospheres altering oxide chemistry, or poor BN dispersion that prevents tribofilm continuity. Above ~900 °C, accelerated BN oxidation or softening of the matrix may change behavior.
generation.uncertainty: Exact magnitudes of friction and wear reductions depend on BN volume fraction, platelet size and orientation, composite porosity, counterface chemistry, and humidity. The continuity of the BN/B2O3 tribofilm at 800 °C in air and its persistence under higher loads has not been verified for CoCrFeNi and may vary with processing.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two pin-on-disk specimens: (1) baseline CoCrFeNi alloy as described; (2) CoCrFeNi + 5 vol% h-BN composite produced by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering to ≥98% relative density, polished to identical finish. Use an alumina counterface and test in laboratory air (30–50% RH). Measure coefficient of friction and specific wear rate at 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C under 10 N load and 0.1 m/s sliding speed for 2000 m per temperature. After each test, analyze the wear track tribofilm via Raman spectroscopy/XPS and cross-sectional TEM to detect BN/B2O3 and assess film continuity.
measurements: Steady-state coefficient of friction at each temperature
Specific wear rate of the alloy and counterface at each temperature
Tribofilm composition (BN, B2O3, Co/Cr/Ni oxides) and continuity by Raman/XPS/TEM
Hardness of the composite versus baseline
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if at any tested temperature within 25–800 °C under the stated conditions: (a) the composite’s steady-state coefficient of friction is not at least 20% lower than the baseline, or (b) the composite’s specific wear rate is not at least 2× lower than the baseline, or (c) no BN/B2O3-rich tribofilm is detected on the composite’s wear track.
